rationale: Both candidates independently rediscover that the ground-truth's sole concern (trust_remote_code breaking locked kernels 0.13.x installs) was already resolved by commit 9947f414, but Y states the causal mechanism precisely ('older get_kernel doesn't accept the kwarg, which would have made every fallback attempt fail') matching the GT reasoning, while X buries the same insight under ~10 near-duplicate 'Validated'/'claim-refuted' log entries and 4 nearly-identical inline comments restating the same PR-description staleness point, hurting signal density. Y adds genuinely new, well-grounded findings (sticky cache of transient failures via broad except, dead-code fallback branch on kernels>=0.15, missing cache-reset hook) with appropriate hedging on less-verifiable claims (CI gate), whereas X's unique findings (cache poisoning without validation, CI lane coverage) are solid but diluted by redundancy. Both are reasonably actionable with file/line refs, X even supplies literal patch suggestions, but Y's overall higher signal-to-noise and deeper technical correctness give it the edge.
